newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas jumps in brief Q1 frenzy, dips back late.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas jumps in brief Q1 frenzy, dips back late.

text.p: UK spot natural gas markets closed firmer in the winter on Thursday, traders and brokers said, although the first quarter next year was well down on its highest levels by the close.

In what was described as "a mad 20 minutes" at around 1400 GMT, the Q1 price jumped quickly to 17.10 pence a therm, where it was traded at least twice and possibly more. After these trades, a bid/offer spread of 17.15/17.25 pence a therm was briefly seen in the market, but prices soon slipped.
Within a few minutes all the heat had gone out of the quarter and it fell back to a bid/offer spread of 16.80/16.90 pence a therm, where the market closed.

During the brief Q1 frenzy, a St Fergus seller reported getting a bid at 16.10 pence a therm. As a result the seller raised the offer to 16.60 pence from 16.50 pence, although there was another lower offer heard at 16.50 pence. But it was not thought that trade was concluded there as bids and offers remained too far apart.

Q4 also ended the day slightly firmer on the offer and the gas year, which was actively traded, ended stronger as well, but most periods were stable. In addition to the reported trades, it was rumoured that deals were concluded at 10.90 pence a therm for a Q2/Q3 strip, at 11.45 pence twice for Q2, and at 12.90 pence and 12.95 pence twice for the October 1997 gas year.
And one company reported trading a January/February strip at "well over 18 pence," but declined to give any further details.

A trader who attended the Network Code meeting on Thursday afternoon reported that shippers encouraged Transco to buy and sell more regularly on the flexibility mechanism as this would avoid "gaming opportunities" now often seen on the mechanism.
He added that there was a hope that Transco would act "in a more mechanistic and predictable fashion."
The IPE futures market saw 200 lots traded, all in the winter and all at higher prices, in line with the movements seen on the OTC market.
